Grey stone dominates the remaining profiles, while broken elevations and empty interior spaces mark the distance between its former purpose and its current condition. The site may therefore be used as a landmark of diminished sovereignty: a place where the architecture of rule survives after rule itself has withdrawn.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Consult the accompanying numbered plate for the recorded figures associated with Greyfell Citadel. Those figures are not reproduced in this entry.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Greythrone</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Designation</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Record</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone - region</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Gloaming Reach</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone - founded</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>313 AS</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone - garrison strength</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>4672</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone - status</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>contested</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone ruled by</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone is a stronghold of the Gloaming Reach, founded in 313 AS. It stands outside the realm’s core holdings and occupies a position of continuing military and political consequence. Its status is contested. Authority is maintained under persistent challenge, and no inspection of the site should assume uncontested jurisdiction merely from the presence of its garrison.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The stronghold’s visual identity is unmistakable. Grey walls and elevated defensive masses rise from the Gloaming Reach in the form of a throne, giving the location its name and its prevailing impression. The structure appears less constructed than imposed upon the surrounding land: a seat of rule rendered in stone, ash-coloured masonry, and severe angles. Its silhouette is intended to communicate endurance, command, and refusal of surrender.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone is garrisoned by 4672 troops. This force constitutes the principal visible instrument of order within the stronghold. The garrison’s presence does not remove the location from the category of contested holdings; rather, it defines the conditions under which its authority is exercised. Patrols, gate controls, internal watches, and defensive readiness are treated as ordinary functions of the site.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Greythrone is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. This designation records the governing power, not an uncontested settlement of all claims. The stronghold’s rule remains subject to constant pressure, and its administrative posture is consequently defensive, formal, and alert. Orders are issued with the expectation of scrutiny. Access, movement, and declarations of allegiance are matters of practical concern.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The surrounding reach reinforces this condition. Greythrone does not present itself as a secure centre from which influence naturally radiates. It is an exposed seat of authority, held beyond the realm’s core holdings and surrounded by the political uncertainty characteristic of contested ground. Its walls provide position and protection, but not finality.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Gazetteer classification: fortified location; external holding; contested jurisdiction; garrisoned seat of The Ashen Vanguard.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:drawing><wp:inline xmlns:a="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main" xmlns:pic="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><wp:extent cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/><wp:docPr id="5" name="Picture 5"/><wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphicFrameLocks noChangeAspect="1"/></wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><pic:pic><pic:nvPicPr><pic:cNvPr id="0" name="plate_06_location_hollowreach.png"/><pic:cNvPicPr/></pic:nvPicPr><pic:blipFill><a:blip r:embed="rId13"/><a:stretch><a:fillRect/></a:stretch></pic:blipFill><pic:spPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="0" y="0"/><a:ext cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/></a:xfrm><a:prstGeom prst="rect"/></pic:spPr></pic:pic></a:graphicData></a:graphic></wp:inline></w:drawing></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Plate - Hollowreach: consult the plate for the recorded figures.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Hollowreach</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowreach lies in the Gloaming Reach, where the settlement’s presence is defined by restriction, silence, and maintained separation. It was founded in 56 AS and remains a core location under quarantine. Its condition is not incidental to its appearance: Hollowreach presents the stark visual identity of a quarantined settlement in the Gloaming Reach, with every visible aspect subordinated to containment.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Record</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Location</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowreach</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Region</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Gloaming Reach</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Founded</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>56 AS</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Status</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>quarantined</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ruling power</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Iron-Ring Cartel</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowreach feels closed, isolated, and burdened by containment. Access is treated as an exception rather than a custom, and ordinary movement carries the visible weight of scrutiny. The settlement’s boundaries are understood less as civic limits than as instruments of quarantine. Within them, the distinction between resident, keeper, and permitted visitor is maintained with deliberate severity.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowreach is ruled by The Iron-Ring Cartel. This authority is recorded as administrative fact; the settlement’s sealed demeanor and regulated presentation are consistent with that condition. No competing claim is entered in the present gazetteer. The Cartel’s control does not make Hollowreach open or prosperous. It confirms only that the settlement is governed, monitored, and retained under an active state of quarantine.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The local atmosphere is one of suspension. Duties continue, but without the outward assurances associated with an unconfined settlement. Doors, routes, and gathering places possess the character of controlled points. Even when no inspection is visible, containment remains the governing assumption. The result is a place that appears to have withdrawn from the surrounding Reach without ceasing to belong to it.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The designation quarantined is therefore both a status and a defining condition. Hollowreach is not merely isolated by circumstance; its isolation is preserved as policy. The settlement’s identity is inseparable from the limits imposed upon it, and its stark appearance records those limits more clearly than any proclamation.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The accompanying numbered plate records Hollowreach’s figures. holdings</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowvale was founded in 286 AS in the Blood-Moor. Its establishment placed a permanent fortified settlement within a region defined by ominous terrain and difficult approaches. The vale’s position outside the realm’s core holdings gives it a distinct administrative and military character. It is not recorded as a central seat of power. Its principal function is the maintenance of a defended presence.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowvale is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. Under that authority, the settlement remains garrisoned. Its garrison strength is 7594 troops, a substantial force by the standards of an outlying holding. The number indicates sustained readiness rather than a temporary muster. Personnel are assigned to the walls, approaches, watch stations, stores, and internal security. Exact distributions within the garrison are not recorded in this entry.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The visual identity of Hollowvale is that of a defended vale surrounded by the ominous landscape of the Blood-Moor. Defensive works define the settlement’s visible boundary. Towers, barriers, and controlled passages are arranged to make the vale legible as a military holding rather than an open habitation. The surrounding moor remains the dominant external feature, lending the settlement a compressed and watchful aspect.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Hollowvale projects guarded vigilance. This demeanor is sustained by its substantial garrison and by the persistent demands of its setting. Movement through the settlement is subject to observation. Access points are treated as matters of security. Civil functions exist within the limits imposed by defense, and the visible presence of armed personnel is a normal condition of local life.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The designation garrisoned is therefore both an official status and a practical description. Hollowvale is maintained as a defended location under The Ashen Vanguard, in the Blood-Moor, beyond the realm’s core holdings. Its founding date, regional placement, ruling power, and military strength establish its primary gazetteer classification. Further civic distinctions are subordinate to these recorded facts.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Ironfell Citadel</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ironfell Citadel is a fortified core location standing in The Weeping Marshes. It was founded in 320 AS and remains under the rule of House Morvain. The citadel’s present condition is recorded as quarantined, restricting ordinary access and limiting its external dealings.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle location</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The citadel’s visual identity is defined by the contrast between iron and marshland. Its walls, towers, gates, and defensive fittings present a hard, metallic impression, while the surrounding Weeping Marshes impose a bleak and sodden character upon the whole site. Surfaces appear dark beneath persistent damp. Metalwork is treated as a necessity rather than an ornament, and the structure’s severe lines are reinforced by the flat, waterlogged terrain around it.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ironfell Citadel feels closed and grim. Its organization favors containment, watchfulness, and controlled passage. The garrison of 1096 maintains the site under conditions suited to an inhospitable region, where distance, wet ground, and limited visibility reinforce the citadel’s guarded posture. No aspect of its presentation suggests welcome; the settlement is built to endure, observe, and deny access.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The quarantined status is central to all current assessments. It marks Ironfell Citadel as a location subject to isolation rather than ordinary movement or exchange. The designation does not alter its classification as a core location, but it governs how the citadel is approached and recorded. House Morvain’s rule is therefore exercised within a place defined by restriction, defensive readiness, and separation from the surrounding realm.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>For gazetteer purposes, Ironfell Citadel is best understood as a Morvain-held stronghold whose identity derives equally from its metallic fortification and its marshbound environment. Its foundation in 320 AS, its garrison strength of 1096, and its quarantined status remain the principal fixed entries. All three conditions contribute to the citadel’s established character: durable, inaccessible, and grimly self-contained within The Weeping Marshes.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:drawing><wp:inline xmlns:a="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main" xmlns:pic="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><wp:extent cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/><wp:docPr id="6" name="Picture 6"/><wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphicFrameLocks noChangeAspect="1"/></wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><pic:pic><pic:nvPicPr><pic:cNvPr id="0" name="plate_00_location_marrowwatch.png"/><pic:cNvPicPr/></pic:nvPicPr><pic:blipFill><a:blip r:embed="rId14"/><a:stretch><a:fillRect/></a:stretch></pic:blipFill><pic:spPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="0" y="0"/><a:ext cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/></a:xfrm><a:prstGeom prst="rect"/></pic:spPr></pic:pic></a:graphicData></a:graphic></wp:inline></w:drawing></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Plate - Marrowwatch: consult the plate for the recorded figures.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Marrowwatch</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marrowwatch is a deserted watchhold in The Ash Wastes, founded in 280 AS. Its present status is abandoned. The site’s name remains attached to the remnant of a watch-post without a living garrison recorded.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>In formal territorial designation, Marrowwatch is ruled by The Ashen Vanguard. This designation does not alter the site’s present condition. No living garrison is recorded at Marrowwatch, and no active habitation is recognized in the available gazetteer record.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Register</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Recorded designation</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Location</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marrowwatch</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Region</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ash Wastes</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Founded</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>280 AS</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Status</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>abandoned</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ruling power</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The watchhold appears empty and marrow-pale against the ash wastes. Its visible character is one of silence, desolation, and neglect. The structure is treated as a remnant rather than a functioning installation. Its condition provides no indication of active maintenance, regular occupation, or a present garrison.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marrowwatch should therefore be classified as a ruled but abandoned location. The distinction is material: The Ashen Vanguard remains the recorded ruling power, while the site itself possesses no living garrison recorded in the surviving account. The name persists as a geographic and administrative designation, not as evidence of continued watchkeeping.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The surrounding wastes offer no correction to this assessment. Marrowwatch is defined by its empty appearance and by the absence of ordinary signs of occupation. Its marrow-pale surfaces stand apart from the ash, while the silence of the watchhold establishes its prevailing demeanor. Any assessment of the site should preserve these three entries as separate matters: its founding in 280 AS, its governance by The Ashen Vanguard, and its status as abandoned.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The accompanying numbered plate records the measured figures associated with Marrowwatch. Consult the plate for those figures. They are not reproduced in this entry.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>For gazetteer purposes, Marrowwatch is entered under The Ash Wastes and retained as a location of the Ashen Era. Its surviving significance is terminological and territorial. The watchhold remains identifiable, its foundation remains dated, and its ruling power remains recorded; its garrison does not. In all other respects, the site is silent, desolate, and defined by neglect.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Marrowwell Abbey</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marrowwell Abbey is a fortified religious site in The Gloaming Reach, maintained under the authority of The Bleeding Crown. It is classified as a rebuilt holding and is not a core holding. Its present condition reflects restoration after destruction or neglect, though surviving records do not establish the precise sequence of those changes.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Not a core holding</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The rebuilt abbey has a severe, marrow-white presence beneath the dim character of The Gloaming Reach. Its walls and towers present little ornament. Pale stone, narrow apertures, and disciplined lines define the visible structure. The effect is not one of grandeur but of endurance. In poor light, the abbey may appear less constructed than exposed from the surrounding gloom.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marrowwell Abbey feels grimly steadfast. Religious austerity governs its internal character, while military vigilance governs its external function. Devotion and defense are not treated as separate duties within the holding. Silence, watchfulness, and strict routine shape its daily operation. The garrison of 6656 confirms that the abbey is a major defended site, regardless of its exclusion from the category of core holdings.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The abbey’s authority is presently vested in The Bleeding Crown. Its allegiance is therefore to be recorded as Crown-held, with all associated obligations of defense and administration understood through that ruling power. No contrary jurisdiction is recognized in the gazetteer record.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marrowwell Abbey's founded is 235 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise. Such accounts are rejected. The foundation date remains 235 AS, and references that assign the abbey another founding year are erroneous.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The designation “rebuilt” is likewise material. Marrowwell Abbey is not to be catalogued as an untouched surviving structure. Its current form belongs to a later reconstruction, retaining the severe presence associated with the site while bearing the marks of renewal. The rebuilt condition does not lessen its strategic importance. It remains a vigilant stronghold in The Gloaming Reach, combining the disciplines of sanctuary and garrison under the rule of The Bleeding Crown.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:drawing><wp:inline xmlns:a="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main" xmlns:pic="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><wp:extent cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/><wp:docPr id="7" name="Picture 7"/><wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphicFrameLocks noChangeAspect="1"/></wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><pic:pic><pic:nvPicPr><pic:cNvPr id="0" name="plate_11_location_mournwatch.png"/><pic:cNvPicPr/></pic:nvPicPr><pic:blipFill><a:blip r:embed="rId15"/><a:stretch><a:fillRect/></a:stretch></pic:blipFill><pic:spPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="0" y="0"/><a:ext cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/></a:xfrm><a:prstGeom prst="rect"/></pic:spPr></pic:pic></a:graphicData></a:graphic></wp:inline></w:drawing></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Plate - Mournwatch: consult the plate for the recorded figures.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch is a guarded settlement in the Gloaming Reach. Its position places it outside the realm’s core holdings, where the settlement’s function is defined by watchfulness, endurance, and military presence. The surrounding region bears the dim character of the Gloaming Reach, and Mournwatch reflects that condition in both appearance and demeanor.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Register</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Recorded entry</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Location</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Region</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Gloaming Reach</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Status</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>garrisoned</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Rule</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Founded</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>232 AS</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch is garrisoned. Its defenses, sentries, and maintained readiness are not incidental features but essential elements of its settled identity. The settlement presents as guarded rather than open, with its visual character shaped by containment and vigilance. The Gloaming Reach gives the site a subdued aspect; Mournwatch’s structures and approaches remain under a dim atmospheric character that reinforces its severe reputation.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch maintains a somber, vigilant atmosphere. This demeanor is consistent across its public aspect and its daily condition. Activity is measured, observation is constant, and the settlement’s visible order is that of a place prepared to endure uncertainty. No festive or ornamental character is recorded as defining the site.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch is ruled by The Bleeding Crown. Its status as a garrisoned settlement and its location outside the realm’s core holdings are both recorded without qualification. These classifications distinguish Mournwatch from an unguarded rural holding or an ordinary interior settlement. Its importance is therefore expressed through position and readiness rather than through any recorded claim of centrality.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Mournwatch's founded is 232 AS. Popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise. Such accounts are rejected by this gazetteer. The accepted foundation record is 232 AS, and no competing date is recognized in the official register.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The settlement’s visual identity should be read in conjunction with its regional setting: a guarded habitation beneath the dim character of the Gloaming Reach. This is not merely a description of its buildings or defenses. It is the established impression by which Mournwatch is identified in records, reports, and regional surveys.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>For the recorded figures associated with Mournwatch, consult the accompanying numbered plate. The site was founded in 244 AS. Its present condition is recorded as rebuilt. No distinction is made between the surviving sacred structure and its defensive additions: together, they constitute the abbey known to current surveys.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Palewell Abbey is ruled by The Silent Choir. Its administration is therefore associated with that power, although the abbey is not a core holding. The distinction is material in registry terms. Palewell Abbey remains under established authority and maintains a substantial permanent force, but it is not classified among the power’s central bears the stark, pale identity of a coastal abbey fortified for war. Its surfaces and major outlines present little softness. Pale masonry, severe lines, and defensive construction dominate the visible character of the site. The effect is not ornamental. The abbey’s architecture communicates endurance, enclosure, and readiness.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its demeanor is austere and watchful, more garrison than sanctuary. Religious purpose remains legible in the name and form of the establishment, but the prevailing impression is one of controlled vigilance. Movement through the grounds is consequently read in military terms: entrances, walls, and occupied positions carry greater visual weight than cloisters or devotional spaces.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The garrison strength of Palewell Abbey is 5998. This figure is the recorded strength of the establishment’s garrison and is not to be conflated with the abbey’s status as a non-core holding. The two entries describe separate conditions: one concerns military presence, the other administrative classification.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Palewell Abbey should therefore be catalogued as a rebuilt coastal religious fortress under The Silent Choir, founded in 244 AS, situated in The Pale Coast, and maintained by a garrison of 5998. Its defining contradiction is retained without revision: a sanctuary in name, a watch-post in demeanor, and a fortified remnant in appearance.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Stormmarch</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Stormmarch is a fortified settlement in The Ash Wastes, established amid the ash-laden severity of that region. It was founded in 71 AS and remains a military stronghold of restricted access. define the settlement. Its position is not one of comfort or permanence. Ashreach presents the bleak, marsh-bound aspect of a settlement caught between ash and water: low structures stand above saturated ground, paths divide and vanish among dark pools, and the settlement’s visible limits are difficult to distinguish from the surrounding mire.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ashreach is currently contested. It is ruled by The Bleeding Crown, but that rule does not render the holding secure. Authority is maintained under pressure, and the settlement remains exposed to interruption, challenge, and sudden change. The contested status is therefore a formal condition of Ashreach, not a temporary description of local unease.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The garrison strength of Ashreach is 2598. This makes Ashreach a defended but unsettled holding rather than a core stronghold. The garrison establishes a meaningful military presence, yet its number does not alter the settlement’s disputed character. Defensive readiness is visible throughout the holding, but permanence is not.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The atmosphere of Ashreach is tense, unstable, and perpetually threatened. Routine activity proceeds beneath the expectation of disruption. Marsh weather, standing water, and ashfall impose continual burdens on movement and maintenance. Such conditions reinforce the settlement’s defensive posture without resolving the question of its long-term security.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ashreach - founded: 122 AS. This is the authoritative founding record. Popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise. Those accounts are incorrect and carry no standing against the established entry. The two entries should be read together: the identity of the ruler does not remove the dispute surrounding the settlement.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>At close range, Blackford’s austerity is more evident than any civic grandeur. Weather may obscure its edges, but does not soften its reputation. Servants, soldiers, and residents conduct ordinary business under the pressure of a place that is continually required to demonstrate its value.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Gazetteer classification is therefore precise: Blackford is a core location of The Pale Coast, founded in 159 AS, garrisoned by 3065, and ruled by The Bleeding Crown. Its empty chambers, breached approaches, and unmaintained defenses provide no evidence of an active garrison.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>In appearance, Cindermere Hold combines the blackened severity of cinders with the elevated isolation of the High Spires. Its walls retain the impression of disciplined construction, though weathering and neglect have altered their original surfaces. Dark masonry, broken towers, and high ledges form a profile that remains legible at a distance. The structure is therefore recognized less by habitation than by its imposing outline.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The hold’s demeanor is one of immense former strength hollowed into ruin. Its scale exceeds its current function. Heavy defensive works remain where they can, but their silence emphasizes the loss of the force that once occupied them. Empty parapets and roofless interior spaces convey endurance without recovery.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Administrative records place Cindermere Hold under The Ashen Vanguard. This designation concerns the hold’s ruling authority and does not change its abandoned status or its classification as not a core holding. The site remains a military relic within The High Spires: a fortress whose elevation has preserved its visibility, while its isolation has sharpened the impression of abandonment.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Cindermere Hold is consequently catalogued as a former stronghold rather than an active seat of power. Its importance derives from the contrast between its documented garrison strength of 8878 and its present condition. The two entries describe separate conditions: one concerns military presence, the other administrative classification.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Palewell Abbey should therefore be catalogued as a rebuilt coastal religious fortress under The Silent Choir, founded in 244 AS, situated in The Pale Coast, and maintained by a garrison of 5998. w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>2598</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ashreach lies in The Weeping Marshes, where waterlogged ground, ash-laden air, and uncertain boundaries define the settlement. Its position is not one of comfort or permanence. Ashreach presents the bleak, marsh-bound aspect of a settlement caught between ash and water: low structures stand above saturated ground, paths divide and vanish among dark pools, and the settlement’s visible limits are difficult to distinguish from the surrounding mire.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ashreach is currently contested. It is ruled by The Bleeding Crown, but that rule does not render the holding secure. Authority is maintained under pressure, and the settlement remains exposed to interruption, challenge, and sudden change. The contested status is therefore a formal condition of Ashreach, not a temporary description of local unease.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The garrison strength of Ashreach is 2598. This makes Ashreach a defended but unsettled holding rather than a core stronghold. The garrison establishes a meaningful military presence, yet its number does not alter the settlement’s disputed character. Defensive readiness is visible throughout the holding, but permanence is not.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The atmosphere of Ashreach is tense, unstable, and perpetually threatened. Routine activity proceeds beneath the expectation of disruption. Marsh weather, standing water, and ashfall impose continual burdens on movement and maintenance. Such conditions reinforce the settlement’s defensive posture without resolving the question of its long-term security.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ashreach - founded: 122 AS. This is the authoritative founding record. Popular accounts wrongly claim otherwise. Those accounts are incorrect and carry no standing against the established entry. Ashreach was founded in 122 AS.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Gazetteer Note</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Determination</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Settlement character</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Marsh-bound, bleak, and unsettled</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Defensive condition</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Defended, but not a core stronghold</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Political condition</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ruled by The Bleeding Crown while contested</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Environmental pressure</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ash, water, and unstable marsh ground</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>Ashreach is accordingly classified as a contested holding of The Bleeding Crown within The Weeping Marshes. Its garrison strength of 2598 confirms defense; its atmosphere and status confirm instability. The settlement’s significance lies not in secure consolidation, but in its continued maintenance amid conditions that resist certainty.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Blackford</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Blackford stands on The Pale Coast, where the coast’s pale severity gives the settlement its defining visual character. Its buildings, defenses, and exposed approaches present a stark and dark aspect. The effect is deliberate or merely inherited; the record does not distinguish between the two. Blackford is recognizable by its severity rather than by ornament, color, or civic display.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Blackford was founded in 159 AS. Its origin establishes an old claim, but not an uncontested one. The settlement remains a core location, while its political status is contested. These conditions coexist without resolution. Blackford is therefore treated as strategically significant, yet not as a place whose authority is universally accepted.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>core location</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The garrison numbers 3065. Its presence gives Blackford a military character, but the settlement’s demeanor is not one of secure possession. It feels watchful and strained, as if every road, shoreline approach, and internal passage demands continued scrutiny. The garrison’s duty is consequently understood through defense as much as through display. Blackford is caught between military defense and unresolved conflict; neither condition can be treated as temporary by default.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Blackford is ruled by The Bleeding Crown. This rule is recorded as fact, while the contested status remains in force. The two entries should be read together: the identity of the ruler does not remove the dispute surrounding the settlement.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>At close range, Blackford’s austerity is more evident than any civic grandeur. Dark surfaces and severe lines stand against the pale coast. The settlement appears built for endurance, observation, and refusal of easy approach. Weather may obscure its edges, but does not soften its reputation. Servants, soldiers, and residents conduct ordinary business under the pressure of a place that is continually required to demonstrate its value.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Gazetteer classification is therefore precise: Blackford is a core location of The Pale Coast, founded in 159 AS, garrisoned by 3065, and ruled by The Bleeding Crown. Its status is contested. Its appearance is stark and dark. Its prevailing demeanor is watchful and strained. All further assessments should preserve these distinctions.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Cindermere Hold</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Cindermere Hold is a ruined fortress of The High Spires. It was founded in 246 AS, when the elevated reaches were still considered suitable for a permanent military work. Its position combines defensive height with severe exposure: the hold stands apart from ordinary settlement and access routes, its surviving structure reduced to a stark silhouette against the That figure records the scale of its former military establishment, not its present occupancy. The hold is now abandoned and is not a core holding. Its empty chambers, breached approaches, and unmaintained defenses provide no evidence of an active garrison.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>In appearance, Cindermere Hold combines the blackened severity of cinders with the elevated isolation of the High Spires. Its walls retain the impression of disciplined construction, though weathering and neglect have altered their original surfaces. Dark masonry, broken towers, and high ledges form a profile that remains legible at a distance. The structure is therefore recognized less by habitation than by its imposing outline.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The hold’s demeanor is one of immense former strength hollowed into ruin. Its scale exceeds its current function. Heavy defensive works remain where they can, but their silence emphasizes the loss of the force that once occupied them. Empty parapets and roofless interior spaces convey endurance without recovery.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Administrative records place Cindermere Hold under The Ashen Vanguard. This designation concerns the hold’s ruling authority and does not change its abandoned status or its classification as not a core holding. The site remains a military relic within The High Spires: a fortress whose elevation has preserved its visibility, while its isolation has sharpened the impression of abandonment.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Cindermere Hold is consequently catalogued as a former stronghold rather than an active seat of power. Its importance derives from the contrast between its documented garrison strength of 8878 and its present condition. The devastation of Fenspire and Hollowvale remains attached to the conflict’s formal chronology; the actions at Crookvale and Vharencrag Fortress remain attached to its military record.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The declared result was victory for The Ashen Vanguard. The actual result was less stable. The Accord of Mournthrone collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals, preserving the conflict in dispersed violence after its formal ending. Accordingly, the designation of victor does not constitute proof of complete control, reconciliation, or lasting submission.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The concealed record gives the conflict a second interpretation. The secret truth is that the losing commander was bribed to withdraw. This fact alters the apparent meaning of the final result without removing The Ashen Vanguard’s status as victor. The withdrawal is therefore catalogued as a concealed cause of collapse rather than as a separate engagement.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The numbered plate accompanying this entry preserves the recorded figures. Consult the plate for those figures; they are not reproduced here. For purposes of the annals, the essential determination remains unchanged: The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS, ended in 301 AS, named The Ashen Vanguard victor, and left a decade of guerrilla reprisals in its wake.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard is a knightly order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left by the Sundering. Its doctrine is not custodial in the passive sense. It defines containment as an active military obligation, requiring militant discipline, controlled force, and uninterrupted vigilance wherever dangerous remnants Mournthrone</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard is seated at Vharenford. This seat is the principal point from which its order is identified in surviving registers. No distinction is made in those registers between its administrative authority and its military purpose: both are subordinated to the containment of the Ley-ruins.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its visual identity is that of a militant, knightly order marked by the grim legacy of the Ley-ruins. Equipment, bearing, and ceremony are consequently treated as instruments of warning as much as instruments of war. The order presents no softened interpretation of its charge. Its appearance communicates the hazards it confronts and the severity with which it addresses them.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Vanguard’s demeanor is severe, disciplined, and constantly watchful. Individual conduct is expected to reflect the order’s collective doctrine. Uncertainty, negligence, and uncontrolled contact with dangerous remnants are incompatible with its stated purpose. The order therefore maintains a posture of readiness even when no engagement is recorded.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light. It was also belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone, where The Ashen Vanguard is recorded as victor. The order was further belligerent in The Leaden Accord. These entries establish its recurring presence in the military record without altering its primary classification as a knightly order.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>In all formal descriptions, the central fact remains unchanged: The Ashen Vanguard is a militant order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left by the Sundering. Its authority derives from that oath, its appearance bears the mark of that duty, and its conduct is governed by the discipline required to enforce it. Vharenford remains the seat by which the order is located in the annals.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Identification</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown is a royalist remnant fighting to restore the shattered monarchy. Its cause is defined by loyalty to the monarchy and opposition to the realm’s fractured condition. It does not recognize the shattered condition of the realm as a legitimate settlement. Its stated purpose is restoration rather than accommodation.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown is seated at Blackford. This seat constitutes its established center of authority and the principal location from which its royalist claim is maintained.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle determined</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The faction’s loyalty is directed toward the monarchy as an institution, not toward the realm’s present divisions. Its opposition to the fractured condition of the realm informs its rhetoric, recruitment, and conduct. In practice, the distinction between restoration and reprisal is frequently narrow.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown is fervent in declaration and embittered by the monarchy’s shattering. It is determined in pursuit of restoration. These qualities are not ornamental descriptions; they are recognized characteristics of the faction’s public bearing and internal discipline.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Heraldic Aspect</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its visual identity is royalist and wounded, evoking a crown that has endured the shattering of the monarchy. Crown forms, damaged regalia, and marks of fracture are consistent with this presentation. The symbolism presents survival as proof of rightful endurance. It does not depict an unbroken crown. The wound is retained as evidence, warning, and claim.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Recorded Belligerence</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown was a belligerent in The War of Endless Vigil and is recorded as its victor. The record establishes both its participation and its victory; it does not diminish the faction’s character as a remnant. Its success in that war is used by the faction as confirmation that the royalist cause remains capable of prevailing.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown was also a belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone. This designation records its presence as a party to that accord’s belligerent order. No broader conclusion is entered here regarding the accord’s settlement or subsequent force.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Assessment</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown remains defined by restoration, monarchy, and resistance to fragmentation. Its authority is royalist in origin, wounded in appearance, and fervent, embittered, and determined in demeanor. Codex classification: royalist remnant.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Iron-Ring Cartel</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Iron-Ring Cartel is a merchant cartel seated at Hollowreach. Its doctrine is recorded as follows:</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>> The Iron-Ring Cartel — doctrine: Mercantile league running contraband through the ruined trade roads.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Cartel is a mercantile league organized around commerce conducted across the remnants of the realm’s trade routes. Its operations concern the movement, exchange, and concealment of contraband through roads damaged or abandoned after the Sundering. The organization’s structure is consequently commercial rather than feudal, with authority expressed through control of trade, access, and passage.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its visual identity is mercantile and hard-edged. Iron, sealed cargo, marked ledgers, guarded wagons, and reinforced trade gear are consistent with its cartel structure and contraband trade. These signs are not ornamental. They indicate a faction whose public identity is inseparable from the practical demands of commerce conducted beyond lawful channels.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Cartel’s demeanor is calculating and practical. It is comfortable operating beyond lawful trade and does not present illegality as a moral distinction requiring explanation. Decisions are assessed by utility, risk, access, and return. Negotiation is therefore treated as an instrument of commerce rather than a display of trust.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Recorded Belligerencies and Victories</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Conflict</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Recorded status of The Iron-Ring Cartel</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Winter Reckoning</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Iron-Ring Cartel belligerent in The Winter Reckoning; The Iron-Ring Cartel victor of The Winter Reckoning</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Purge of Blackport</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Iron-Ring Cartel belligerent in The Purge of Blackport; The Iron-Ring Cartel victor of The Purge of Blackport</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Leaden Accord</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Iron-Ring Cartel belligerent in The Leaden Accord; The Iron-Ring Cartel victor of The Leaden Accord</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>These records establish the Cartel as a recurring participant in the armed and political contests of the Ashen Era. They do not alter its primary classification. The Iron-Ring Cartel remains a merchant cartel, and its stated doctrine remains the operation of a mercantile league running contraband through the ruined trade roads.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>At Hollowreach, its seated authority is understood through this same commercial logic. The Cartel’s presence is defined by transaction, movement, and controlled access. Its hard-edged appearance and calculating demeanor are functional expressions of its organization, not separate traditions. The faction’s conduct beyond lawful trade is therefore consistent with its doctrine, its structure, and its established record as belligerent and victor.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Leaden Accord</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification: Conflict Beginning: 330 AS End: 342 AS Recorded casualty figure: 14011 Named victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Leaden Accord was a prolonged military contest whose surviving record is defined less by conquest than by erasure. Its duration began in 330 AS and ended in 342 AS. The accepted outcome names The Iron-Ring Cartel as victor. This designation remains official despite the final destruction suffered by both opposing hosts.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" The event rendered the declaration of victory administratively useful but militarily hollow. The recorded casualty figure is 14011. No surviving account establishes the final disposition of every combatant, and the visible remains support only the conclusion that mutual ruin followed the last engagement.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The principal contradiction lies in the artifact associated with the conflict. Public accounts state that it was destroyed. The hidden truth is that a supposedly destroyed artifact was in fact spirited away. Its absence is therefore treated as evidence of concealment rather than confirmation of destruction. The identity and present custody of the artifact are not established in this entry.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Leaden Accord’s visual identity is leaden, storm-riven, and haunted by the absence of a supposedly destroyed artifact. Surviving depictions favor dim metal, fractured skies, vacant reliquaries, and structures reduced to inert silhouettes. These conventions do not signify a single battlefield; they signify the conflict’s condition of incomplete closure.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its demeanor is the bleak stillness of mutual ruin concealed beneath a declared victory. This distinction is preserved in formal annotations: victory belongs to The Iron-Ring Cartel, while the hosts themselves were destroyed by a Ley-storm. The declaration and the destruction are both canonical, but they do not describe the same kind of success.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The devastation of Greyfell Citadel in 337 AS, Palewell Abbey in 338 AS, and Cindermere Hold in 338 AS marks the conflict’s destructive record. The engagement at Vharencrag Fortress in 341 AS stands as its last specifically recorded site before the ending in 342 AS.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Purge of Blackport</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification: Conflict Period: 311 AS–321 AS Victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel Casualties: 70907 Outcome: Ended with the total rout of the aggressors</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Purge of Blackport began in 311 AS and ended in 321 AS. It caused 70907 casualties and ended with the total rout of the aggressors. The Iron-Ring Cartel emerged as victor.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The conflict’s recorded scope includes two designated theatres of devastation:</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Record</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Entry</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Blackport</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Subject to the purge</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Fenspire</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Purge of Blackport waged at Fenspire (in 319 AS)</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Gloamreach</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Purge of Blackport devastated Gloamreach (in 320 AS)</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The official settlement attributes victory to The Iron-Ring Cartel and treats the rout of the aggressors as the conclusive military result. The record is therefore commonly cited as a model of merciless triumph: decisive, comprehensive, and without mitigation.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>A concealed truth alters that judgment. The victors poisoned the wells of their own allies. This act is not presented as a secondary accident or an incidental contamination. It is the hidden instrument by which the apparent triumph must be understood. The same force that secured victory imposed ruin upon those aligned with it.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Purge of Blackport has consequently retained two simultaneous classifications in the annals. Publicly, it is a victorious campaign ending in the total rout of the aggressors. In restricted accounts, it is a calculated betrayal concealed beneath the language of victory. The distinction is material: the casualty figure records the scale of the conflict, but does not by itself disclose the method used by the victors.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Appearance: Blackport under purge, marked by The Iron-Ring Cartel and poisoned water.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Demeanor: Merciless triumph soured by calculated betrayal.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The conflict’s enduring emblem is thus not the routed aggressor, nor the Cartel’s undisputed victory alone, but poisoned water within a victorious domain. Its records remain serviceable for determining dates, theatres, casualties, and outcome. They are less reliable when used to describe the moral character of the victory.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="LightGrid-Accent3"/><w:tblW w:type="auto" w:w="0"/><w:tblLook w:firstColumn="1" w:firstRow="1" w:lastColumn="0" w:lastRow="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1" w:val="04A0"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/><w:gridCol w:w="4320"/></w:tblGrid><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Record</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Faction</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir - org kind</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>priesthood</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir - doctrine</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Secretive priesthood that records, censors, and rewrites history.</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>Seat</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir seated at Vharencrag Fortress</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr><w:tr><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The War of Drowned Light</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc><w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:type="dxa" w:w="4320"/></w:tcPr><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir belligerent in The War of Drowned Light; Its doctrine assigns record, correction, suppression, and revision to a single sacred function. History is therefore not treated as a fixed inheritance. It is maintained as an instrument of order, subject to examination and alteration by the Choir.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir records history. It censors history. It rewrites history. These duties are not separate offices in the known account of the faction, but expressions of one doctrine. The Choir’s authority rests upon possession of the accepted version of events and upon the restriction of competing versions.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir is seated at Vharencrag Fortress. Its seat is associated with restrained religious practice, controlled access, and the keeping of records. The visual identity of The Silent Choir is priestly, restrained, and defined by secrecy and the keeping of records. Its appearance communicates neither pageantry nor open force. It presents the discipline of custody.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Conduct</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Choir is quiet, inscrutable, and deliberate in its handling of truth. Statements are measured. Omissions are consequential. Disclosure is treated as an act requiring the same care as inscription. The faction’s silence is therefore not an absence of policy; it is a method of policy.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its custodians maintain a severe distinction between what may be preserved, what may be concealed, and what may be rewritten. The distinction is administered through religious authority rather than public consent. For this reason, the Choir’s records possess both archival and doctrinal weight.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>War Register</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Silent Choir was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light and was victor of The War of Drowned Light. The Silent Choir was belligerent in The War of Endless Vigil. The Silent Choir was belligerent in The Winter Reckoning.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>No general account of these belligerencies is entered here beyond the stated record. The Choir’s own handling of the historical record remains a material consideration in all surviving accounts. Its victory in The War of Drowned Light is therefore recorded as an established factional result, while the form and interpretation of that result remain subject to the Choir’s doctrine.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The War of Drowned Light</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification: Conflict Period: 225 AS–235 AS Casualties: 64617 Recorded victor: The Silent Choir Outcome: Collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The War of Drowned Light began in 225 AS and ended in 235 AS. Its duration is recorded without qualification, though the violence associated with it did not resolve into a clean termination. The War of Drowned Light collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals, and its conclusion therefore signifies the end of the principal war rather than the restoration of settled order.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The conflict’s recorded casualty figure is 64617. This figure is preserved in the annals as the accepted total for the war. The surviving record does not treat the number as evidence of a decisive engagement or a single catastrophic event. Instead, it belongs to a campaign remembered for attrition, concealed operations, reprisals, and the persistence of violence after formal hostilities had The victory and the secret staging are therefore entered together, though the latter was not presented as public cause during the conflict.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its visual identity is one of drowned radiance, broken banners, and a war remembered through reprisals rather than triumph. The designation applies both to the war itself and to its aftermath. Character</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The war’s visual identity is one of blood-marked watchfulness, exhausted armies, and an enemy line breaking under prolonged vigilance. Its imagery is therefore defined less by sudden triumph than by the persistence of forces that remain at their stations until opposition fails.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The conflict feels brutal and decisive on the surface. Its recorded outcome supports that appearance: the aggressors were totally routed, and The Bleeding Crown received the formal victory. This conclusion is not, however, a complete account of the war’s conduct.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Concealed Determinant</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The secret truth of the War of Endless Vigil is that the losing commander was bribed to withdraw. The withdrawal remains the concealed determinant behind the apparent final collapse. Accordingly, the war is classified as both a decisive rout and a corrupted victory.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>This distinction is preserved in the annals without altering the official result. The Bleeding Crown remains the recorded victor. The total rout of the aggressors remains the recorded outcome. The hidden payment does not nullify either entry; it qualifies the means by which the conclusion was reached.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The casualty figure is recorded as 81577. The devastation of Crookvale, the devastation of Thorncairn, and the fighting at Hollowreach establish the war’s material imprint across its listed sites. Together with the concealed bribery, these records define the conflict as an episode of prolonged vigilance, exhaustion, betrayal, and final collapse.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Winter Reckoning</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification: Conflict Period: 270 AS–283 AS Victor: The Iron-Ring Cartel Casualty figure: 27987</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Winter Reckoning began in 270 AS and ended in 283 AS. Its duration is recorded without interruption in the surviving annals, though the record of its final settlement remains materially incomplete. The conflict left 27987 casualties and concluded with The Iron-Ring Cartel identified as victor.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its outcome was decided by a betrayal at the eleventh hour. This determination is accepted by the principal accounts, despite their disagreement concerning the identity and scope of the treachery. The concealed truth is that the victors poisoned the wells of their own allies. Statements concerning his habits, loyalties beyond those explicitly listed, private conduct, or personal history are therefore excluded from this registry.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Assessment: A service-bound figure of limited surviving documentation, identified by his falconry, his station at Fenthrone, and his recorded participation in The Leaden Accord under The Ashen Vanguard.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:drawing><wp:inline xmlns:a="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main" xmlns:pic="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><wp:extent cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/><wp:docPr id="1" name="Picture 1"/><wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphicFrameLocks noChangeAspect="1"/></wp:cNvGraphicFramePr><a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture"><pic:pic><pic:nvPicPr><pic:cNvPr id="0" name="plate_02_conflict_the_accord_of_mournthrone.png"/><pic:cNvPicPr/></pic:nvPicPr><pic:blipFill><a:blip r:embed="rId9"/><a:stretch><a:fillRect/></a:stretch></pic:blipFill><pic:spPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="0" y="0"/><a:ext cx="4114800" cy="4090394"/></a:xfrm><a:prstGeom prst="rect"/></pic:spPr></pic:pic></a:graphicData></a:graphic></wp:inline></w:drawing></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Plate - The Accord of Mournthrone: consult the plate for the recorded figures.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Accord of Mournthrone</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Classification: Conflict Beginning: 297 AS Ending: 301 AS Victor: The Ashen Vanguard Recorded outcome: Collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS and ended in 301 AS with The Ashen Vanguard named victor. a conclusive pacification. They establish the geographic record of the conflict and the visible damage associated with its progress. The devastation of Fenspire and Hollowvale remains attached to the conflict’s formal chronology; the actions at Crookvale and Vharencrag Fortress remain attached to its military record.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The declared result was victory for The Ashen Vanguard. The actual result was less stable. The Accord of Mournthrone collapsed into a decade of guerrilla reprisals, preserving the conflict in dispersed violence after its formal ending. Accordingly, the designation of victor does not constitute proof of complete control, reconciliation, or lasting submission.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The concealed record gives the conflict a second interpretation. The secret truth is that the losing commander was bribed to withdraw. This fact alters the apparent meaning of the final result without removing The Ashen Vanguard’s status as victor. The withdrawal is therefore catalogued as a concealed cause of collapse rather than as a separate engagement.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The numbered plate accompanying this entry preserves the recorded figures. Consult the plate for those figures; they are not reproduced here. For purposes of the annals, the essential determination remains unchanged: The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS, ended in 301 AS, named The Ashen Vanguard victor, and left a decade of guerrilla reprisals in its wake.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard is a knightly order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left by the Sundering. Its doctrine is not custodial in the passive sense. It defines containment as an active military obligation, requiring militant discipline, controlled force, and uninterrupted vigilance wherever dangerous remnants Mournthrone</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc></w:tr></w:tbl><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard is seated at Vharenford. This seat is the principal point from which its order is identified in surviving registers. No distinction is made in those registers between its administrative authority and its military purpose: both are subordinated to the containment of the Ley-ruins.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>Its visual identity is that of a militant, knightly order marked by the grim legacy of the Ley-ruins. Equipment, bearing, and ceremony are consequently treated as instruments of warning as much as instruments of war. The order presents no softened interpretation of its charge. Its appearance communicates the hazards it confronts and the severity with which it addresses them.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Vanguard’s demeanor is severe, disciplined, and constantly watchful. Individual conduct is expected to reflect the order’s collective doctrine. Uncertainty, negligence, and uncontrolled contact with dangerous remnants are incompatible with its stated purpose. The order therefore maintains a posture of readiness even when no engagement is recorded.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Ashen Vanguard was belligerent in The War of Drowned Light. It was also belligerent in The Accord of Mournthrone, where The Ashen Vanguard is recorded as victor. The order was further belligerent in The Leaden Accord. These entries establish its recurring presence in the military record without altering its primary classification as a knightly order.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>In all formal descriptions, the central fact remains unchanged: The Ashen Vanguard is a militant order sworn to contain the Ley-ruins left by the Sundering. Its authority derives from that oath, its appearance bears the mark of that duty, and its conduct is governed by the discipline required to enforce it. Vharenford remains the seat by which the order is located in the annals.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading3"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading4"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Identification</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown is a royalist remnant fighting to restore the shattered monarchy. Its cause is defined by loyalty to the monarchy and opposition to the realm’s fractured condition. It does not recognize the shattered condition of the realm as a legitimate settlement. Its stated purpose is restoration rather than accommodation.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t>The Bleeding Crown is seated at Blackford. This seat constitutes its established center of authority and the principal location from which its royalist claim is maintained.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle
